patents.source: USPTO Open Data Portal, granted patents since 2001, applicant phrase "alphabet", 2026-10-05

reading.body:
Alphabet's public record here is a corporate shell: filings, a ticker, and 281 California cases, with no products, no MCP servers, and no AI positioning in its own words.

The data covers the SEC filing cadence from May to August 2026, eight filings in four months, and 23 granted patents since 2001. That patent set is not an AI portfolio. The recent titles concern electronic communications accounts keyed to physical addresses, plus one composition for common colds. Nothing in the patent record speaks to compute, data centers, or power.

For AI specifically, this tells a reader almost nothing. Alphabet is one of the largest builders of AI infrastructure, but the facts given contain no data center count, no megawatts, no capital expenditure, and no grid interconnection. The 281 California cases are a count without subject matter, so they cannot be tied to energy contracts, land use, or utility disputes.

What the data does establish is scale of legal exposure in one state and a steady filing habit. It does not establish what Alphabet builds, what it consumes, or where its compute sits. Any claim about Alphabet as a power buyer would have to come from somewhere other than this record.

profile_text.body:
Alphabet is a public company founded in 2015 and headquartered in Mountain View, California. It trades under the ticker GOOGL and files with the SEC under CIK 0001652044. Its website is abc.xyz, where the material available is its investor relations home page.

The held facts record no AI products tracked for Alphabet and no MCP servers. No lawsuits are listed. The law exposure record shows 281 cases in California.
